Root Cause Analysis: KubePodCrashLooping — api pods in shop namespace

CONFIRMED ROOT CAUSE

The api Deployment's liveness probe is misconfigured to check port 8081, but the application only ever listens on port 8080. Every ~60-70s the kubelet kills the container with SIGKILL after 3 failed liveness checks, producing the crash loop.

Evidence chain

Symptom confirmed in real time: kubectl get pods -n shop shows api-c7b987b4d-f98rz and api-c7b987b4d-mbfs7 with RESTARTS 1 (63s ago) / 1 (62s ago) at only ~2m age — actively restarting.
Events show the mechanism: 
   Liveness probe failed: Get "http://10.244.2.33:8081/healthz": dial tcp 10.244.2.33:8081: connect: connection refused → Killing ... Container api failed liveness probe, will be restarted. Readiness probe on port 8080, by contrast, succeeds (200 in app logs).
Deployment spec confirms the mismatch: kubectl get deployment api -n shop -o yaml → livenessProbe.httpGet.port: 8081 vs readinessProbe.httpGet.port: 8080 and containerPort: 8080. Notably the kubectl.kubernetes.io/last-applied-configuration annotation (the originally-applied manifest) shows liveness also on port 8080 — meaning someone later patched/edited only the live object's liveness port to 8081 without updating the applied config (deployment.kubernetes.io/revision: "2", i.e. this is revision 2, not the original).
Pod-level confirmation: kubectl describe pod shows Port: 8080/TCP, Liveness: http-get http://:8081/healthz, and Last State: Terminated, Reason: Error, Exit Code: 137 at 17:04:07/08 — a kubelet-initiated SIGKILL, not an application crash or OOM (OOM would show Reason: OOMKilled).
Application code confirms single-port design: ConfigMap api-code → api.py binds ThreadingHTTPServer(("", PORT), H) where PORT = int(os.environ.get("PORT", "8080")). No env var PORT is set in the pod spec, so it binds only 8080. There is no second listener on 8081 anywhere in the code.
Resource exhaustion ruled out: kubectl top pods -n shop shows api pods using 4m CPU
